chunk_findings.detail: The retry window is a hard 4 x 0.1 s = 400 ms, and nothing in the loop requires the file to be making progress — it neither requires the count to increase between looks nor extends the deadline while the writer is still writing. The transient it is meant to absorb is exactly a rewrite that has a duration: an in-place git rewrite of a shard that is larger than the modest ones in the bug report (or the same shard on a slow/loaded filesystem, or with the rewriting process descheduled between write chunks) leaves the reader looking at a truncated file for longer than 400 ms. Concretely: a shard with ~20k events (the size the guidance cites, where a scan is already ~7 ms) is checked out on a loaded CI machine; the reader lands in the `O_TRUNC` window at t=0 and the writer has produced fewer than `old["count"]` events at t=0.1/0.2/0.3/0.4; `_settled` returns the short scan, the caller's re-check at lines ~230-236 is still true, and `out[key] = {**old, "shrunk": True}` is written. The mark is sticky, so the doctor reports "lost events" for a shard that is whole a moment later — i.e. B-events-uncommitted-shards reproduces with a slower writer. A deadline that only ends when two consecutive looks read the same count (with a much larger cap) is what the stated promise ("a real loss is still there") needs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/shardmarks.py `_settled` (added retry block, ~lines 192-209)

chunk_findings.detail: A transient *disappearance* of the shard is treated as the signal to stop trying, which is the opposite of settling. Git (and any rotation/rewrite path that unlinks before creating) has a window in which the working-tree file does not exist; if the rescan inside `_settled` lands there, `_scan` returns `None`, the loop breaks immediately, and the *stale* truncated tuple from the first look is returned. The caller then evaluates `_holds(path, seen)` against the live filesystem — if the file has already been recreated whole, `_holds` is true but `scanned[0]` is the stale short count, so `out[key] = {**old, "shrunk": True}` is still written for a shard that is complete at the moment of the decision. Input that demonstrates it: first look sees the truncated shard (count 50 of 100), the writer unlinks/rewrites, the in-loop rescan at +100 ms gets `OSError` -> `None`, the file reappears whole before the caller's `_holds` check. `_settled` should re-scan (or treat `None` as "keep waiting up to the deadline") instead of committing a shrink based on a snapshot it already knows was taken mid-write.

chunk_findings.detail:
The test's settling is injected via `monkeypatch.setattr(shardmarks.time, "sleep", lambda s: path.write_text(whole))`, and the replacement ignores its argument and restores the file on the very first call. The test therefore passes for any value of the constants that actually decide whether the bug is fixed: with `SETTLE_S = 0.0`, or `SETTLE_LOOKS = 1`, or a window of 1 ns, the lambda still fires once, the rescan still sees the whole file, and the assertions stay green — while in production those settings leave the `O_TRUNC` window completely unabsorbed and the original `shrunk` notice returns. Since the fix is entirely a timing heuristic, the regression test pins only "a retry exists", not "the retry is long enough", so it cannot detect the regression it is supposed to prevent. (The same line also rebinds the stdlib `time` module's `sleep` process-wide for the duration of the test, because `shardmarks.time` *is* the `time` module.)

Note on the other half of the intent: the manifest touches only the shrink/`lost` path; nothing in this change addresses the "uncommitted event shards" symptom, so if that symptom has an independent cause it is left unfixed. I could not establish that from the diff alone, so I am not raising it as a finding.

chunk_findings.detail: For a document with exactly one region the two arms of `_region_digest` are indistinguishable: `mine[0].sha` (line 104) returns the begin-marker sha, and the fallback `W._region_pattern(doc, "begin").group("sha")` (line 112) also returns the begin-marker sha of the single marker. The new test therefore passes even if the whole `if mine:`/multi-region arm added by this change is deleted, or if `RC.regions` returns `[]` and only the fallback runs — so the new logic (the combined `F.body_digest("name=sha\n"…)` digest, its line format, its helper) ships with zero coverage. Concretely, feed it a region document with two regions for the same doc (e.g. `roadmap/index` and `roadmap/log`): the multi-region branch is the only thing that runs, and a wrong concatenation or a bad `F.body_digest` call would still leave CI green. The expected value is also derived with the same `RC.regions` parser, on the same file, that the implementation uses, so the assertion reduces to "the parser returns the same string twice": if the writer ever records a sha that is not the digest of the region body (a stale sha, or another region's sha), the test cannot tell.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_doc_region_refresh.py:198

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback is the only code that runs when `mine` is empty — i.e. exactly for a region-mode document whose marker carries no usable sha, the case the fallback exists for — and it reaches into a private helper of another module and assumes a capture-group contract that this change neither establishes nor tests: `W._region_pattern(doc, "begin").search(text)` followed by `.group("sha")`. Nothing pins that the write module's *begin* pattern (whose job is to locate the marker in order to splice it) exposes a group named `sha`. If it does not, `.group("sha")` raises `IndexError`, and `_digest_of`'s handler — `except (OSError, ValueError, ExportError)`, unchanged by this diff — does not catch it, so the previously harmless "no digest" degradation becomes an uncaught exception that aborts the whole `refresh_selected` call for that document.

data.question: why do critic/rubber_duck verdicts change 8-11 times on one item

chunk_findings.detail: The proposed detector rule and its regression test contradict each other, and the rule does not actually remove the false positive on the items under study. The rule is "count a flip only when ... a `gate.started` between the two outcomes." Applied to the fix-Ba24a8d32ee sequence the document itself gives — failed 17:01, passed 17:09 (settlement, explicitly "no review started in between"), failed 17:21 — the adjacency passed(17:09)→failed(17:21) *does* have a `gate.started` between its two outcomes (the review that failed at 17:21), so it is still counted as a flip. Six such rounds therefore still yield ~5 flips (one per settlement→next-failure boundary), not zero; the doc's claim that the printed advice "is wrong for these items, which did converge" is not delivered by the stated fix. Concretely for the regression test as written — "a failed review round followed by a triage pass, repeated five times, is not `gate_flapping`" — the emitted outcome sequence is F1,P1,F2,P2,F3,P3,F4,P4,F5,P5; each P_i→F_{i+1} transition has a `gate.started` between the two outcomes and is counted, giving 4 flips, so the test's first assertion fails unless the flapping threshold happens to exceed 4, which is not stated and would also leave the 11-flip item flagged after the fix. To match the test, settlement passes would have to be filtered out of the outcome stream entirely (not merely checked for an intervening `started`), which is not what the rule says.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/gate-flapping.md (Fix section, lines ~41-48)

chunk_findings.detail: The quantitative summary mislabels its own figures: "All 4475 recorded critic/rubber_duck outcomes: 2538 failed, 680 passed on a clean review (0 findings), 1257 passed otherwise (triage, budget, refutation)" and then "A third of the gate's passes are settlements." The passes are 680 + 1257 = 1937, so the settlement share is 1257/1937 ≈ 65%, roughly two thirds, not one third. 1257/4475 ≈ 28% only if the denominator is *all outcomes*, not "the gate's passes." The sentence as written overstates the convergence argument the verdict rests on by roughly a factor of two (the claim "exactly the shape that reads as a flip" is backed by ~65%, not ~33%, of passes).

The new test therefore passes even if the whole `if mine:`/multi-region arm added by this change is deleted, or if `RC.regions` returns `[]` and only the fallback runs — so the new logic (the combined `F.body_digest("name=sha\n"…)` digest, its line format, its helper) ships with zero coverage. Concretely, feed it a region document with two regions for the same doc (e.g. `roadmap/index` and `roadmap/log`): the multi-region branch is the only thing that runs, and a wrong concatenation or a bad `F.body_digest` call would still leave CI green. The expected value is also derived with the same `RC.regions` parser, on the same file, that the implementation uses, so the assertion reduces to "the parser returns the same string twice": if the writer ever records a sha that is not the digest of the region body (a stale sha, or another region's sha), the test cannot tell.

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback is the only code that runs when `mine` is empty — i.e. exactly for a region-mode document whose marker carries no usable sha, the case the fallback exists for — and it reaches into a private helper of another module and assumes a capture-group contract that this change neither establishes nor tests: `W._region_pattern(doc, "begin").search(text)` followed by `.group("sha")`. Nothing pins that the write module's *begin* pattern (whose job is to locate the marker in order to splice it) exposes a group named `sha`. If it does not, `.group("sha")` raises `IndexError`, and `_digest_of`'s handler — `except (OSError, ValueError, ExportError)`, unchanged by this diff — does not catch it, so the previously harmless "no digest" degradation becomes an uncaught exception that aborts the whole `refresh_selected` call for that document.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/refresh.py:112

chunk_findings.detail: `IndexError` is added to the blanket `except` that wraps the *whole* decision block, not just the region path. That try block contains `return _region_digest(text, doc)` — which itself reaches into `W._region_pattern(doc, "begin").search(text)` and `.group("sha")`, and `re.Match.group(name)` raises `IndexError` ("no such group") for any name the pattern does not define — as well as `RC.regions(...)` and, on the non-region path, `F.split(text)`. Every `IndexError` raised anywhere inside that block is now converted into `return ""`, i.e. a falsy digest. A falsy digest is exactly what `Refresh.evidence()['digests']` drops, which is the reported symptom of Bb850be2a85 ("region documents contribute no digest to refresh evidence"): so for any input that makes region parsing or the marker group lookup index out of range (e.g. a region-mode document whose begin marker is present but whose marker/body is truncated, so the parse indexes a missing element, or a generated frame whose header is short enough that `F.split` indexes past the end), the refresh now silently records no digest and treats the document as unchanged instead of surfacing the malformed input — the bug the change claims to fix is reproduced in a quieter form. Because this single catch also covers the "no markers" case asserted by the new test (`RF._region_digest("no markers\n", "d") == ""`), that assertion can be satisfied by exception swallowing rather than by an explicit no-marker branch, so it does not pin which condition produces the empty digest.

chunk_findings.detail:
The new sixth argument looks the partial findings up by the chunk's *position inside `wanted`* rather than by its chunk index. `_retry_truncated` is only handed `retried`, which is built as `[wanted[k] - 1 ...]` — i.e. 0-based chunk indices — so the `partial` map it fills is keyed by chunk index (that is also why `partial.get(n - 1)` would be the matching lookup). The two coincide only when `wanted == [1, 2, ..., N]`; on the documented `only` code path (`only` names the chunks to send, `merge_rerun` folds the run into the full record) they diverge.

Concrete failure: `run_review(..., only=[2, 5])` where both chunk 2 and chunk 5 are lost to size after the split rounds. `retried` is `[1, 4]`, so `partial` is `{1: <findings of chunk 2>, 4: <findings of chunk 5>}`. The absorb loop then does, for `n=2`, `partial.get(wanted.index(2)) = partial.get(0)` → `None` (chunk 2 silently loses its partial findings), and for `n=5`, `partial.get(wanted.index(5)) = partial.get(1)` → chunk 2's findings, which are then absorbed into `res` for chunk 5 / `files[4]`. The rerun therefore reports the wrong findings against the wrong file (and drops the real ones), and `merge_rerun` carries that corruption into the full run's record. The full-range run used by the new tests never exposes this, because there `wanted.index(n) == n - 1`.

chunk_findings.detail: The retry window is a hard 4 x 0.1 s = 400 ms, and nothing in the loop requires the file to be making progress — it neither requires the count to increase between looks nor extends the deadline while the writer is still writing. The transient it is meant to absorb is exactly a rewrite that has a duration: an in-place git rewrite of a shard that is larger than the modest ones in the bug report (or the same shard on a slow/loaded filesystem, or with the rewriting process descheduled between write chunks) leaves the reader looking at a truncated file for longer than 400 ms. Concretely: a shard with ~20k events (the size the guidance cites, where a scan is already ~7 ms) is checked out on a loaded CI machine; the reader lands in the `O_TRUNC` window at t=0 and the writer has produced fewer than `old["count"]` events at t=0.1/0.2/0.3/0.4; `_settled` returns the short scan, the caller's re-check at lines ~230-236 is still true, and `out[key] = {**old, "shrunk": True}` is written. The mark is sticky, so the doctor reports "lost events" for a shard that is whole a moment later — i.e. B-events-uncommitted-shards reproduces with a slower writer. A deadline that only ends when two consecutive looks read the same count (with a much larger cap) is what the stated promise ("a real loss is still there") needs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/shardmarks.py `_settled` (added retry block, ~lines 192-209)

chunk_findings.detail: A transient *disappearance* of the shard is treated as the signal to stop trying, which is the opposite of settling. Git (and any rotation/rewrite path that unlinks before creating) has a window in which the working-tree file does not exist; if the rescan inside `_settled` lands there, `_scan` returns `None`, the loop breaks immediately, and the *stale* truncated tuple from the first look is returned. The caller then evaluates `_holds(path, seen)` against the live filesystem — if the file has already been recreated whole, `_holds` is true but `scanned[0]` is the stale short count, so `out[key] = {**old, "shrunk": True}` is still written for a shard that is complete at the moment of the decision. Input that demonstrates it: first look sees the truncated shard (count 50 of 100), the writer unlinks/rewrites, the in-loop rescan at +100 ms gets `OSError` -> `None`, the file reappears whole before the caller's `_holds` check. `_settled` should re-scan (or treat `None` as "keep waiting up to the deadline") instead of committing a shrink based on a snapshot it already knows was taken mid-write.

chunk_findings.detail:
The test's settling is injected via `monkeypatch.setattr(shardmarks.time, "sleep", lambda s: path.write_text(whole))`, and the replacement ignores its argument and restores the file on the very first call. The test therefore passes for any value of the constants that actually decide whether the bug is fixed: with `SETTLE_S = 0.0`, or `SETTLE_LOOKS = 1`, or a window of 1 ns, the lambda still fires once, the rescan still sees the whole file, and the assertions stay green — while in production those settings leave the `O_TRUNC` window completely unabsorbed and the original `shrunk` notice returns. Since the fix is entirely a timing heuristic, the regression test pins only "a retry exists", not "the retry is long enough", so it cannot detect the regression it is supposed to prevent. (The same line also rebinds the stdlib `time` module's `sleep` process-wide for the duration of the test, because `shardmarks.time` *is* the `time` module.)

Note on the other half of the intent: the manifest touches only the shrink/`lost` path; nothing in this change addresses the "uncommitted event shards" symptom, so if that symptom has an independent cause it is left unfixed. I could not establish that from the diff alone, so I am not raising it as a finding.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_shard_high_water.py `test_a_shard_caught_half_rewritten_by_git_is_not_flagged_as_lost`

chunk_findings.detail: The probe offered for prior finding 1 ("progress-aware window") does not exercise progress. `_caught_short(..., restore_on_sleep=3)` keeps the truncated file *byte-identical* across the first two sleeps and then snaps it to `whole` on the third, so the retry loop sees no partial progress at all; and the companion never-settling test only asserts a lower bound (`n >= 4`). Any implementation whose window is a plain fixed block of >= 4 looks — i.e. no extension while the writer is still writing, which is exactly the defect prior finding 1 described — passes both tests: look1 short, sleep1, look2 short, sleep2, look3 short, sleep3 (restore), look4 whole -> `n == 3`, `lost` false. Conversely the never-settling case gives `n == 4` for the same fixed window. So if the progress-extension part of the fix in `shardmarks.py` were reverted (or never actually implemented), this suite would stay green; the tests only establish "the window is at least 4 looks", which is what the original bug needed, not the progress-awareness the triage claims.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_shard_high_water.py `test_a_shard_caught_half_rewritten_by_git_is_not_flagged_as_lost`

chunk_findings.detail: Both new tests only simulate an *in-place truncation* (`path.write_text(...half...)`); neither ever unlinks the shard. Prior finding 2 was specifically about the git/rotation window in which the working-tree file does not exist, where the rescan returns `None`, and the triage claims the fix makes "a vanished file count as a look". With no test that removes and recreates the shard mid-`_settled`, reverting that branch (e.g. back to `if again is None: break`) leaves this suite fully green, since a `None` rescan never occurs in these two scenarios. The regression the fix claims to close for the vanish-then-recreate case is therefore not guarded by the added tests.

chunk_findings.detail: The branch that marks a shard shrunk no longer goes through `_settled`. A single half-rewritten look is enough to produce `{**old, "shrunk": True}`. For example, `coordinator.jsonl` has an `old` mark with count 10; git has currently written only five events, so `_scan` returns count 5 and this branch immediately emits a shrunk row. After git writes the remaining events, the row stays `shrunk` on this run, which is exactly the false lost notice the fix is meant to remove. The other two added `_settled` calls are guarded by `not row.get("shrunk")`, so they cannot clear this flag on the same run.

chunk_findings.detail: The “progress-aware” window still has a hard 4 × 0.1 s no-progress stop: `quiet` is incremented whenever `_scan` returns `None` or the same byte size. A writer descheduled between two chunks, or git not yet recreating a file after unlink for ≥ 0.4 s, makes `quiet >= looks`; the loop exits at the top without a fifth, completed look and returns the stale short tuple. The shard would later have been whole, so the previously reported descheduled-window/long-unlink defeat remains.
